input: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production (scheduled routine)
task: open-tennis-robots (flagship 10): the slip hub facing's friction spread with wear as a sweep axis

doc_friction.issue: Tells you to rewrite the venture's `next:`, but for open-tennis-robots the item named 'Next:' is in the `buildable` field. flagship_field.py found it and told me to rerun with --field buildable, which cost one retry.

The slip hub entries treat the disc spring's 400 N flat load as an assumption. DIN 2093's own formula gives 855 N for that size, and the spring's stiffness at the working point (not its flat load) was what the design depended on.

deviations.why: The first route with no --task drew the creative track (weight 0.1). The scheduled brief asks for revenue/venture work, so I routed with --task and got ventures/2 as prompt.md describes.

notes: Wear model: the bench set locks the stack, so facing loss comes off the disc spring's deflection (Almen-Laszlo, checked against the DIN 2093 A 8 row). The single A 12.5x0.7 disc held 4 um of budget; at 40 um worn, a 24 V hot jam with the trip at its highest went uncut on the real firmware. Changed to four B 12.5x0.5 discs in series: 53 um budget against 47 um of assumed loss, every jam cut to 160 um. The boot pocket is now asymmetric and the bench notes add a bed-in and a second set. Verified: tests/test_host 46 OK; cad tests (no build123d) 141 OK with 58 skipped; the full cad suite with build123d and the manufacturing package regeneration are recorded in the PR. No separate agent doc: the next run's item is in flagships.yaml and the method is in cad/README.md.
